title: Reading a card's set record before you buy
target: What a card's own record says about the set it belongs to in TCG Card Shop Simulator, so packs and singles are bought with the set list in view.
version: no version stated by this build (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Cards in the shop or in a pack
The pack screen or a shelf to check against

steps.do: Start from the set a card names rather than from its picture.
steps.because: a card's record names the expansion it belongs to (CardUISetting, expansionType, ECardExpansionType)

steps.do: Treat the set list as fixed rather than as a label you can invent.
steps.because: cards are grouped into a fixed list of named expansions that the game ships (Tetramon, Destiny, Ghost, Megabot, FantasyRPG, CatJob, FoodieGO, Ascension)

steps.do: Read the finish as a second, separate list.
steps.because: a card's finish is a separate fixed list of border styles (ECardBorderType, CardBorder_Base, CardBorder_FirstEdition, CardBorder_Silver, CardBorder_Gold, CardBorder_EX)

steps.do: Expect the artwork to follow the finish.
steps.because: the game ships a border image for each finish, including the full-art frames (CardCenterFrameFullArtMask, CardFrontFullArt_Fire, CardFrontFullArt_Water)

steps.do: Check whether a pack can even use the card's rarity before chasing it.
steps.because: a record says whether an opened pack can use the card's rarity (openPackCanUseRarity)

steps.do: Check whether a pack can contain a duplicate.
steps.because: a record says whether an opened pack can contain a duplicate (openPackCanHaveDuplicate)

steps.do: Know that the artist, the icon and the background are recorded as indices rather than as names.
steps.because: a record carries an artist name index, an icon index and a background index (artistNameIndex, iconIndex, bgIndex)

steps.do: Expect an evolution's icon to be able to come from a different set.
steps.because: a record names a separate expansion for the previous evolution stage's icon (previousEvoStageIconExpansion)

commonMistakes: Assuming a card's set from its border colour alone.
Chasing a rarity the pack you are buying cannot use.
Forgetting that a duplicate is a property of the pack rather than of the card.
Treating the evolution icon as part of the same set as the card.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
